answer_1.quote: The task of code editing aims to resolve errors in given codes to produce a correct solution. Formally, given a problem description q and a defective solution y, our goal is to learn a feedback model θ that generates helpful feedback describing the errors in y and provide helpful guidance on code editing: ĉ = θ(q, y).
answer_1.outputs: natural language feedback for code editing and edited code

answer_2.quote: In evaluating the edited code y ′ , the functionality of the edited code is measured with Pass@k, the standard metric that measures the number of passed test cases t i within the given set T = {t 1 , t 2 , . . . , t k }.

answer_3.quote: For G-Eval, we directly assess feedback quality in Likert-scale (1 -5) using score rubrics.

answer_4.quote: To provide a more accurate analysis of the feedback quality, we conduct human evaluation using qualified workers from MTurk.
answer_4.guideline: We ask human raters from Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) to score the quality of the feedback on a Likert scale.
